characters.name: Sonnie
characters.description: Blue Is Heroic: Sonnie's bioluminescent tattoos glow blue, and she is the most sympathetic character, as a woman who only tries to stay alive, fighting downright despicable people. Butch Lesbian:Played With. Sonnie is plenty beautiful, but she doesn't present a particularly feminine appearance in her style of dress. That being said, her thong straps are visible at all times. Defiant to the End: Even as she lays mortally wounded with most of her head crushed, she taunts Dicko and Jennifer. However, it's subverted in that it's not the end for Sonnie: she's alive within Khanivore, which is her main body from which she controls her human form. Emergency Transformation: After being ripped apart by her kidnappers, her consciousness was placed into Khanivore permanently. Face of a Thug: Sonnie's human face looks quite threatening with all the scars, aKubrick Stareand theDelinquent Hairthat she sports. And yet, she is the good guy, especially when put in contrast with Jennifer, who looks as innocent as a kitten with her baby face and blond hair, and yet is nothing more but a remorseless assassin who works for theBig Badof the story.

characters.name: Ivrina
characters.description: Lady Swears-a-Lot: The most profane female character in the episode. Vapor Wear: She wears an outfit that would even haveJackasking questions. Specifically, its a leather jacket with nothing underneath but glowing bodypaint. Anopenleather jacket. It's not even taped down or anything, since you can catch a brief glimpse ofan areolain a few shots.

characters.name: Khanivore
characters.description: Bizarre Alien Biology: According to the short story, she has no internal organs and has a supply of preoxygenated blood injected before every fight. Confusion Fu: She fights by tiring out its opponents and constantly keeping on her feet, never staying in one place for long and striking from a distance. Combat Tentacles: Her tail splits into four spiked tentacles she can use to walk around on or as very potent weapons. Death by a Thousand Cuts: Her preferred method of combat, as her blows may not be hugely impactful on an individual level, but they'll wear down her foe eventually. Xenomorph Xerox: Khanivore looks like a reptilic xenomorph.

characters.name: Simon
characters.description: Ambiguously Gay: Apparently was checking Flynn out earlier. Though, considering it wasGarywho tells him this, it was likely just a jab. Cruel and Unusual Death:Has his neck torn out by Dracula, before being impaled and torn limb from limb. The Generic Guy: Doesn't have too much to help him stand out from the others. Sacrificial Lamb:Basically just exists to set up how big of a threat Dracula is. Tag Along Kid: By far the youngest and most inexperienced member of the group, being atmostaround his early twenties, and the rest of the group with exception of Wehunt doesn't really take him too seriously.

characters.name: Turboraptor
characters.description: Admiring the Abomination: Team Khanivore can't help but gush about Turboraptor's arm blade. Despite chopping off a piece of Khanivore each time it hit, or perhaps precisely because of that, the team admire how it was a completely legal modification as the blade wasn't metal and they wonder how Turboraptor was modded. Blade Below the Shoulder: After getting his arm torn off, Turboraptor sprouts a blade from the stump. Body Armor as Hit Points: Turboraptor has a thick, almost rocky hide. The hide doesn't reduce or deflect Khanivore's attacks and each time she claws him, a chunk of the hide gets ripped off. But if he didn't have protective hide, her attacks would have gone straight to his vitals. Non-Indicative Name: His name indicates that he is araptor-esqueLightning Bruiser. In reality, while fairly fast, he is more of aMighty Glacier— especially compared to Khanivore — and bears absolutely no resemblance to a raptor.

characters.name: Dicko
characters.description: Big Bad: He's the corrupt owner of the fighting ring and conspires to murder Sonnie after she rejects his offer. A Dick in Name: His name isDicko and he is a bigJerkass. Evil Brit: Downplayed since everyone else in this episode is also British, but his Received Pronunciation accent helps him fit the bill. Evil Cripple: Walks with a limp and uses a heavy cane for support. The sound the cane makes always precedes him. Face Death with Despair: His smugness dissipates and is replaced with fearful whimpers when Sonnie, who is actually in Khanivore's body, gorily kills Jennifer and traps him in her tail, intending to kill him as well.

characters.name: Jennifer
characters.description: Ambiguously Human: It’s left unclear if she’s anArtificial Humanbuilt simply to seduce confident fighters like Sonnie or if herWolverine Clawsare just a small modification to her body. Asshole Victim: Gets brutally murdered by Khanivore after she had just tried to kill Sonnie. Cruelty by Feet: She viciously stomps on Sonnie's impaled head several times to do her in. Dark Action Girl: Very deadly in combat, and serves as Dicko's enforcer/lover. Face of an Angel, Mind of a Demon: She plays the part of a fragile damsel trapped in an abusive relationship which she's too scared to give up, but it's all an act.

characters.name: Announcer
characters.description: Large-Ham Announcer: As befitting someone with his job; he's good at getting the crowd riled up.

characters.name: In General
characters.description: Big, Thin, Short Trio: 11-45-G is the big, XBOT-4000 is the thin, and K-VRC is the short. The Bus Came Back: The trio are the sole characters (as of writing) to gain a sequel episode: Volume 3's "Three Robots: Exit Strategies". Characterization Marches On: The trio's understanding of humanity is far better in "Exit Strategies" compared to their first outing. Before, they barely understood what a basketball was for, while the second episode shows them being more aware about human factions.Justifiedsince, in their first episode, they were simply on vacation taking a tour K-VRC made up. "Exit Strategies" implies they are now doing this as an actual job, and have done more thorough research as a result. Cool Ship: "Exit Strategies" reveals the trio travel around in a sleek, pill shaped ship with anEverything Is an iPod in the Futureaesthetic. Desecrating the Dead: The trio show very little respect for the corpses they encounter.

characters.name: XBOT  4000
characters.description: Audience Surrogate:Inverted; while he is often the one of the group to asks the most questions, they're always ones the audience already knows the answer to. Bland-Name Product: Was anXboxin the original short story. Butt-Monkey: Gets a lot of crap from the other two robots, and is ultimately the one to get stuck with the cat, but takes most of it in stride. Cyber Cyclops:Subverted; the audience first sees him with one eye, but he gains one using the core of his supposed ancestor. Face of a Thug: He resembles your standard, intimidatingMecha-Mook, but he's actually quite genial, if somewhat grumpy.

characters.name: K-VRC
characters.description: Comically Missing the Point: Rarely if ever actually understands the purpose behind common, everyday items. Cute Machines: Is the smallest and most friendly looking of the robots. This is attributed to his product line being descended from a line of baby monitors. The Ditz: Easily the least intelligent of the three robots. Everyone Has Standards: He shows aLack of Empathytowards humans, but afterthe cat shamelessly admits that his species was responsible for the extinction of mankind simply becausethey no longer needed the humans’ help, K-VRC is stunned and says that’s "pretty heartless". Expressive Ears: The potrusions on the side of his head move in ways to accentuate his emotions.

characters.name: 11-45-G
characters.description: Camera Fiend: She's almost constantly taking pictures of everything around her. The Comically Serious: Ironically if you listen to what she's actuallysaying, she's something of aGenki Girl, but her dull monotone voice synthesizer makes her come across like this or aDeadpan Snarker. Deadpan Snarker: She has a text-to-speech program, so a lot of her dialogue comes across as this by default. Dead Person Conversation: She regularly talks to the dead bodies she comes across. Expy: She seems to be one of Siri, with the same voice programming and wikipedic knowledge.

characters.name: The Cat
characters.description: Cats Are Mean:He decides at the end of the short to keep the robots hostage as long as he sees fit. The Elites Jump Ship:They beat the actual elites of humanity in escaping to and colonizing Mars. Killer Rabbit:Despite their cute appearance, it is implied thattheywere the ultimate cause of humanity's extinction; either by slaughtering the surviving humans themselves or by engineering the downfall of humanity as a species sincethey no longer needed humans to open doors and tuna cans. Talking Animal:Although we don't learn about it until the end of the short, all cats were given human speech and intelligence in the past Team Pet: He quickly becomes one for the three robots not so much because they like him as because they're scared of getting rid of him and he keeps following them.

characters.name: Humanity
characters.description: Butt-Monkey: Notonlyhas it been completely wiped from existence, but it also seems to have in the process become little beyond a subject of ridicule from the living robots and cats. Corpse Land: Dead bodies are regularly found just about everywhere, which the robotsdon't even react to. Crapsack World: To say it seems to have gone to shit is a bit of an understatement. Driven to Suicide: One of the bodies they come across seems to have hanged themselves. Hoist by Their Own Petard: In a general sense, and as 11-45-G points out, it ultimately wasn't out-of-control climate change or a nuclear war that ended humanity for good, but its ownstupidityandbastardly selfishnessthat did them in.Or, as the Cat helpfully implies, their own efforts to uplift an animal species that almostimmediatelydecided humans wereno longer necessary for their survivaland thus gleefully let their society implode so saidUplifted Animalspecies could take over.

characters.name: Hank
characters.description: A farmer and central character. Married to Beth. Happily Married: Has a loving relationship with Beth. Huge Guy, Tiny Girl: Hank has a muscular, tall, and broad-shouldered body. His hands even look to be the size of Helen's head when he puts a hand on her back while reassuring her about Jake's death. His wife, Beth, is more petite.

characters.name: Beth
characters.description: Acts as mission control. Married to Hank. Huge Guy, Tiny Girl: Beth has a more petite frame compared to her brawnier husband. Token Minority: The only black main character.

characters.name: Jake
characters.description: Another farmer and is married to Helen. Awesome, but Impractical: His mech is armed with much more sophisticated weapons than Hank or Mel's, but as a result his takes the longest to reload despite having the least reserve ammunition. Draw Aggro: When he realizes his two buddies are going to make a last stand, he charges in to draw theDeeBee's attention while Hank and Mel reload. However he overextends himself and gets flanked, and eventually swarmed. Face Death with Dignity: When he realized how screwed he is, he tells Hank to give his last words to his wife and calmly turns on the suits self destruct. bear in mind this would be pretty dignified on it's ownwithout the horde of screaming bugs on top of him. Small Name, Big Ego: Willingly to admit that he's notMichelangelo, because he thinks of himself as more of ada Vinci...and Hank considers the scarecrow Jake made for him to be categorically awful-looking.Downplayed, since this is really all there is to attest to Jake's ego and Hank later says he's warming up to the scarecrow since it held out as an anchor while he was holding the giantDeeBee's mouth open.

characters.name: Helen
characters.description: Jake's wife who helps out Helen back on the farm. Crusading Widow: After Jake dies she whips out a shotgun and starts shootingDBsherself.

characters.name: Crazy Mel
characters.description: Another farmer who works with Hank and Jake. Boisterous Bruiser: Usually has a grinalong with the cigarin her teeth, Brawn Hilda: She has the personality and the build, though like the others she fights using a mech. Cigar Chomper: She's never seen without a cigar in her teeth, and has the aggressive no-nonsense personality that goes with it. Gender Flip: In the original short story, she was "Crazy Bill," a 70-year-old widower.

characters.name: DeeBees
characters.description: A hostile species of feral aliens who attacked farmers' colonies with goal to kill everyone. Alien Blood: Theirs is a bright yellow-green Horde of Alien Locusts: They come from a breach from outside of the borders, and they come in thousands Insectoid Aliens: They seem to look like spiders with a armor. Zerg Rush: Main strategy to overwhelm the mechs is to use their thousands of numbers.

characters.name: Flynn
characters.description: Anti-Hero: He'sThe Protagonistof the episode, and firmly stands as the most heroic figure in the movie, but nonetheless is a violent mercenary who doesn't really give a damn about the doctors who hired him in the first place to look after them. Deadpan Snarker: Makes it very clear throughout the entire episode that he could not care less about the expedition he was hired onto. Heroic Willpower: Despite its ineffectiveness, he continues to try and kill Dracula with just a tiny little knife. Even Dracula himself seems impressed by this to a degree. Jerk with a Heart of Gold: He may be kind of a dick, but that doesn't mean he doesn't care about his team. The Leader: Leads his team of mercenaries without question, and in return they seem to respect him quite a lot, though not enough to not take occasional jabs at him.

characters.name: Micky
characters.description: Acrofatic: Despite being on the heavy-side, he's certainly fast enough to outruna huge explosion chasing him down. Big Guy, Little Guy: The big guy to Gary's little guy. Brave Scot: Portrays very little to no real fear at the fact they're fightingDracula. The Lancer: Acts as Flynn's second in command for most of the episode. Only Sane Man: Probably the most normal of the three mercenaries.

characters.name: Gary
characters.description: Ambiguously Gay: If her comment is anything to go by, she's into women.Flynn:Little pussy here saved our lives.Gary:Yeah, I know it savedmylife a few times. The Big Guy: By far the most dangerous andAx-Crazymember of the group, with quite a few weapons to boot. Big Guy, Little Guy: The little guy to Micky's big guy. Deadpan Snarker: Just about everything she says is absolutely loaded with sarcasm. Gender-Blender Name: Isseeminglya woman, but is named Gary.

characters.name: Doctor Wehunt
characters.description: Dirty Coward: Ran away the first chance he could from Dracula, leaving Flynn behind in the process. Non-Action Guy: He's a scholar, not a fighter, that's why he has mercenaries. No-Respect Guy: The mercenaries don't respect him all that much due to his cowardice, small body, and cynical outlook on how they're already dead. Only Sane Man: Theonlymember of the group to realize just how screwed they actually are, and how useless their weaponry is against Dracula. The Smart Guy: By far the most intelligent member of the group, which makes sense, as heisa scientist. In fact, his entire motive for hiring the mercenaries in the first place was to protect him while he went to his researching area with his assistant.

characters.name: The Sucker of Souls
characters.description: Adaptational Ugliness.: Nowherenearas handsome as most other interpretations, thoughrather accurate to the original novel. Adaptational Dumbass: Is usually quite intelligent in most major works. Here, he seems to mostly be running on basic survival instincts, though does at least know how to speak. Baddie Flattery: As Flynn continues to attack him, he complements his strong willpower and heart of a warrior. Big Bad: The main antagonist of the episode. Cannibalism Superpower: StartsHulking Outafter drinking Simon's blood, and implies he'll feast on Flynn's heart to gain his warrior courage.

characters.name: Yogurt
characters.description: Yogurt given sentience, and incredible intelligence to boot, who ultimately does more in ten years than whathumanity has done across its entire existence. The Ace: Never makes a single mistake, easily handles issues the rest of the world constantly struggles with, and is an all-around perfect being... Who just so happens to be made of yogurt. Ambiguously Evil: Throughout the episode, it solves the United States' (and later, the world's) economic issues, solves the rest of its issues along the way, and turn it into a peaceful paradise. Despite this, it also acts quite shady inhowit does this, seems to be hiding sinister implications, andhas plans to leave the world behind entirely. Batman Gambit: Seemed topredictthat Congress would ultimately screw up, which leads to it taking control. Big Good: By the end of the episode, it has more or less fixed every major issue that hassles humans today.However, the end of the episodesuggests otherwise.

characters.name: The President of the United States
characters.description: The... President of the United States. The Ditz: Considering he singlehandedly ended up screwing over the economy of the United States (with the exception of Ohio) despite being given clear instructions on how tosolvethe economic crisis, it's made pretty clear he isn't very bright. The Leader: The president and chief decision maker of the United States of America...At least until he hands his position over to yogurt. Lethally Stupid: His own incompetence at his job almost brought an end to the entire country after all. Pride: Seems to believe that he could handle solving the economic issues of the USA without needing to listen toeverythingthe yogurt told him.He thought wrong.

characters.name: The Researchers
characters.description: The very team that ended up bringing the yogurt to life in the first place. Small Role, Big Impact: Has about 20 seconds of total screentime across all of them, and yet they're the ones who brought the yogurt to life in the first place. The Smart Guy: Represented as such for the planet as a whole, being the only humans in the entire episode not portrayed as completely idiotic.

characters.name: The Narrator
characters.description: The narrator of the episode, and the one who recalls all of the events of the story. Casting Gag: The voice actor for The Brain fromPinky and the Brainnarrates a story in which something akin to anUplifted Animaltakes over the world. Deadpan Snarker: He's played byMaurice LaMarche, what are you expecting? Exposition: The entire episode essentially just revolves around him describing how humanity got to where it is in the first place. No Celebrities Were Harmed: Probably unintentional, but he sounds more likeVincent Price.

characters.name: Thom
characters.description: The ship's captain, who encounters an old flame after his crew gets stranded in a remote repair station. Adaptational Nice Guy: Thom is married in the short story and ends up sleeping with Greta while hiding her existence from his wife (or so he thinks he's doing). In the episode, there's no mention that he's married. Ambiguous Situation: While it's clear that Thom is trapped in a simulation for most of the episode and at the very end, it's not clear if the "reality" he sees when he demands to be let in on what's going is truly reality or if it's a simulation meant to reflect it. Greta's exact words are that he's still asleep in his cryo tank. Did You Just Romance Cthulhu?: He spends weeks dating and having sex with "Greta", who's actually the avatar of a grotesque spider-like alien capable of generating false realities within the minds of other creatures. It's unclear what the alien's feelings actually are in this situation, though. Hunk: He's a big muscular man who loses his shirt for a whole scene, and has a fun fling with an old flame. In "reality", he's long since been starved, leaving him bony and emaciated.

characters.name: Suzy
characters.description: The ship's navigator. Only Sane Man: She's very well aware that Greta is not what she seems. Thom is blissfully oblivious, and Ray never actually wakes in Thom's dream. She either represents Thom's subconscious trying to warn him, or is another avatar used by Greta to urge him to face reality. The Smart Guy: She handles the navigation for the ship, which requires complex calculations, lest the ship is thrown off course.

characters.name: Ray
characters.description: The third crewman. Greta insists on keeping him on suspension. Killed Offscreen: After being let out of the simulation, Thom gets a look at his decomposing corpse. Shoo Out the Clowns: He's introduced complaining loudly of a hangover. After the ship is stranded, he's left in his chamber and plays no further role in the story.

characters.name: Greta
characters.description: An old flame of Thom. She's apparently in charge of the repair station Thom and his crew are stuck in. Adaptational Villainy: Downplayed. The original short story makes it unambiguous that the alien impersonating Greta has no ill-will or nefarious goals. That isn't the case here, making her morality more ambiguous though leaning towards being a genuinely empathetic caring alien. Ambiguously Evil: The whole situation seems a bit too suspicious to be coincidence. Greta, meanwhile, seems a bit too reluctant to tell Thom the whole truth. The ambiguity only gets stronger after the reveal ofwhatGreta actually is. It's a horrifying eldritch creature that may or may not have caused the ship to go off course, but why is it so keen on keeping Thom happy? Anti-Villain/Anti-Hero: It's not entirely clear in the episode which one of these she is, thoughWord of Godclaims that she's good, putting her in the latter. She traps ships that have drifted into the void in her snare of meat moss, and traps the victims in a simulation to try to gently break the bad news to them. Her reasons for doing so aren't entirely clear. Apologetic Attacker: In a sense. She's deeply apologetic to Thom, claiming he's not ready to know the truth, but ultimately lets him see a vision of it (she says he's still in his tank, meaning he's never been "truly awake"), and reveals her true self. In this case, she's not even attacking directly, it's just that her very existence and appearance is not healthy for human minds, and she knows it.

characters.name: Liang
characters.description: The protagonist and narrator of the story. The son of a spirit hunter from mainland China, he moves to colonial Hong Kong in search of job opportunities in the growing metropolis. Brainy Brunette: He is a pale dark-haired young man with engineering skills. Character Narrator: He provides most of the narration and exposition in the story. Gadgeteer Genius: Liang has a natural aptitude for machines, and does well in his first job as a railroad worker. By the end of the short, he's making fantastic automatons, and even engineersa new body for Yan that can shift between human and fox forms. Long-Haired Pretty Boy: He lets his hair down by the end of the episode, and is complementing a lot his face.

characters.name: Yan
characters.description: The deuteragonist, and a shapeshiftinghuli jing. Following the death of her mother, she and Liang develop a close friendship and budding romance. However, her new life in Hong Kong results in a traumatic loss of her former identity. Action Girl: After Liang upgrades her cyborg body, she roams around Hong Kong as a vengeful vigilante. Asian Fox Spirit: Yan is ahuli jingand can shift between the form of a human woman and a mystical multi-tailed fox at will. AsThe Magic Goes Away, she undergoesShapeshifter Mode Lockand istrapped in human form. And soon afterwards,she gets stripped of her human form as well. Cybernetic Mythical Beast: At the end of the short, Yan is given an upgraded body able to transform into a cybernetic nine-tailed fox. Cyborg: The Governor forces her to become one until all that's left of her original organic body is her head.

characters.name: Liang's father
characters.description: Liang's late father. He was a spirit hunter who fought and killed various supernatural creatures, including Yan's mother. All There in the Script: His real name is never mentioned but he's credited as Renshu. Anti-Villain: He murders Yan's mother without hesitation or remorse, but only becausehe (wrongly) believes thather kind are inherently dangerous to humans. He's otherwise just aworking father who does this job to provide for his son. Badass Normal: He's an ordinary human who knows how to fight and slay various supernatural creatures. Character Death: He dies offscreen sometime during theTime Skipwhen Liang grows up into a young man. In the original story the short is based on, he wasDriven to Suicidebecause the decline of the supernatural left him without work; he died penniless and largely mocked by the wider community.

characters.name: Tsiao-Jung
characters.description: Yan's deceased mother, who was also ahuli jingjust like her. Ambiguously Evil:Huli jingsare believed toseduce human menfor nefarious purposes. While she does attempt to have sex with a man, she claims to haveneverintended to actually harm him. In any case, her daughter Yan is shown to be a good person; so Liang's father's belief that their species areAlways Chaotic Evilproves to be false, and that his murder of Yan's mother was ultimately pointless. Asian Fox Spirit: A shapeshiftinghuli jingjust like her daughter. Full-Frontal Assault: She is completely naked during the fighting scene with Liang's father, as her clothes disappear as she turns into her half form state. Just like her daughter,she doesn't seem to be ashamed of being completely nude in front of others. Lady of War: She's a notably graceful fighter, swerving and curling around Liang's father in both human and fox forms.

characters.name: The Governor
characters.description: The corrupt British governor of colonial Hong Kong, and a frequent client of Yan when she worked as a prostitute. He has horrifying surgeries conducted on Yan for the sake of satisfying his depraved sexual urges. Antagonistic Governor: To call him aCorrupt Politicianwould be an understatement. He's also a completely insane and amoral rapist, gleefully abusing his power and authority to get away with his vile crimes. Asshole Victim: Given all the terrible things that he did to Yan, there's not a single bit of remorse from her after killing him, nor does Liang question that he really had it coming. Ax-Crazy: His behavior is extremely bizarre and insane even for an evil politician. How many other villains go so far as to kidnap and turn people intocyberneticsex slaves? Big Bad: He's the closest thing to a main villain in this short, though he doesn't last long.

characters.name: Young Hitler
characters.description: A young Hitler living as an aspiring artist in Vienna in 1908. Adolf Hitlarious: Adolf in this depiction is clumsy, awkward, and has an explosive temper (with absolutely no guts to back the latter up). He also dies a lot, in mostly undignified ways. Butt-Monkey: The victim of merciless violence and abuse. Him dying is the literal focus of the short. Oh, Crap!: When he sees two big Jewish men have seen him going on an anti-semitic rant towards a young Jewish boy and another when he sees a meteor about to land on him. They Killed Kenny Again: The running gag of the whole episode. Justified, because these are all hypothetic scenarios.

characters.name: The Jewish Boy
characters.description: A little kid that's very clearly Jewish. He runs afoul of Hitler. Children Are Cruel: Carries apocket knife, which he promptly uses to stab Hitler in the knee right before the adult Jewish men beat him to a pulp in the first death scenario. To be fair, Hitler was beingveryaggressive towards him moments before. Irony: Causes Hitler's death at the hands of two big Jewish men. Then, from the third scenario onwards, hesavesHitler from getting ran over by a horse-drawn cart. Plus, there's the irony of aJewishperson saving the life of Adolf Hitler.

characters.name: The Viennese Prostitutes
characters.description: Four prostitutes that accidentally kill Hitler in a marathonic orgy. They are actuallyinterdimensional ambassadors from a sexy alternate dimension. Gag Penis: One of them is transgender, and has a penis that shows very clearly peeking under her skirt. It then is allowed to wave around freely once the prostitutes reveal themselves as interdimensional travelers. Ms. Fanservice: Well, they're prostitutes from a "sexy alternate dimension", so it's a given.

characters.name: Future Hitler
characters.description: A Hitler from the future that lived to old age. Travels back in time to rescue his younger self from death. Diabolus ex Machina: Comes out of nowhere, kills enemies and allies alike, and saves his younger self, so he can go on and found the Nazi regime - which may or may not have won WWII in his future, considering this Hitler is an old man. This could also be seen as a case ofDeus ex Machina, at least from Hitler's perspective. That is, until hetouches himselfand the ensuing paradox destroys the universe.Ok, not really, it's a simulation after all, so the Multiversity app just crashes. Stupid Jetpack Hitler: A time-traveling Hitler with a bionic eye, piloting alarge robot-suit. Unwanted Assistance: Goes back in time to save his younger self from an assassination attempt. He kills both the assassinsandthe Nazis trying to kill the assassins, since they were at great risk of killing young Hitler with a stray shot.

characters.name: Jibaro
characters.description: Disability Immunity: The main character is deaf and uses sign language to communicate with other humans. As such, he can't be affected by the destructive voice of the siren which drives his fellow soldiers to madness and death. By the end, however, once he drinks the river tainted with the Golden Woman's blood, his hearing is restored... andhis immunity has worn off. Fatal Flaw: Greed. He shows a love of gold and is busy picking bits of it while the other soldiers are preparing, and it eventually culminates in him sticking around the Golden Woman for a chance to strip her gold from her body. As theSole Survivorof her initial attack (thanks to his deafness) and her eventual fondness for him, he very easily could have left the lake and saved his own skin, but after his second encounter with her in which he realizes that the Golden Woman covered in treasure, he chooses to pursue her and steals all of her treasure after knocking her unconscious. First Time Feeling: Jibaro becomes able to hear after stripping the Golden Woman of her gold and drinking the water tainted with her blood, causing him to freak out, and making him vulnerable to her voice. Even worse, its implied that this is his first time hearinganythingbefore. Ironic Name:Jíbarois a Puerto Rican term for self-subsisting farmers who use traditional farming methods. The knight named Jibaro is a colonizer greedy for gold. Sole Survivor: He survived the Golden Woman's first attack because he is deaf and so unaffected by her power. It doesn't last long, as she later exacts her vengeance on him after he mutilates her.

characters.name: The Golden Woman
characters.description: Ambiguously Evil: She kills a ton of soldiers en masse, but considering that they were probably there to steal her gold, it's possible that she did so as a defense mechanism. The short demonstrates that she acts somewhat like an animal, and it's not made clear whether she maliciously kills others or does it on instinct. Ambiguous Situation: Her true feelings towards Jibaro are a bit unclear. While she's clearly attracted to him romantically, is it genuine affection? Is it solely because he is immune to her powers? Does she mistake him for a creature like herself because of his immunity and armor? Or was she planning to still kill him eventually like the others? Attempted Rape: She shows little regard for Jibaro's discomfort when she "seduces" him and even licks her lips after he pushes her off of him. Broken Angel: Visibly despairs seeing her beautiful golden scales have been stolen, along with much of her gems and adornments. This doesn't seem to make her any less powerful as a siren, though. Broken Tears: Has a breakdown after waking up and finding all of her golden missing. She also tearfully compels Jibaro to drown himself.

characters.name: The Army
characters.description: Church Militant: We see several priests that the soldiers kneel before, implying that whatever crusade they are on is at least partially religiously motivated. Given the incredibly looseAnachronism Stewflavor the story establishes, they don't seem to fall under a specific branch of Christianity, but their garbs bring to mind Conquistador-era priests. Cruel and Unusual Death: Along with being forced to drown themselves, some soldiers were also compelled to slice and dice each other, making an already painful and terrifying death even more so. Red Shirt Army: Their deaths establish the Golden Woman's appearance, personality, and powers. Too Dumb to Live: Assuming theywerethere for the Golden Woman, surely they knew about herCompelling Voiceand that it would cause their deaths if they weren't prepared. We Hardly Knew Ye: Aside from a fellow soldier of Jibaro's speaking to him in sign language, and one knight decked out in gold armor and hyping the rest of his team up, none of the soldiers and priests get any defining personalities before dying.
